entries.name: context-map.md
entries.title: Context Map
entries.summary: This repository has one bounded context. It builds authoring assets, not a running product, so there is no second context to integrate with — the hosts that load the assets are outside the boundary.

children.name: domain.md
children.title: Plugin Authoring
children.summary: What this context is responsible for: that an asset written once loads correctly in every host that reads it, and that a plugin can be installed on its own.

children.name: dependencies.md
children.title: Plugin Authoring
children.summary: What this context depends on and who depends on it. The hosts sit outside the boundary and are conformed to; the repositories that adopt a plugin sit outside it and are supplied.

children.name: features.md
children.title: Plugin Authoring
children.summary: What this context lets a maintainer do, in the language of naming.md rather than in file paths. Four features, and each is a thing a host or a consuming repository can observe.

children.name: flow.md
children.title: Plugin Authoring
children.summary: How the terms in model.md move over time: a file becoming something a host loads, payload becoming state in somebody else's repository, and the run a flow skill describes. Structure lives in model.md; responsibilities and boundary live in domain.md.

children.name: model.md
children.title: Plugin Authoring
children.summary: Structural view of the context: what a marketplace holds, what a plugin is made of, and what a plugin leaves behind in a repository that adopts it. domain.md says what the context is responsible for; this file says how its terms relate.

children.name: naming.md
children.title: Naming
children.summary: The terms this repository trades in. Where a host uses a different word for the same thing, the host's word is recorded as an alias rather than adopted.
